issues.detail: The coding-agent section is oriented to Claude Code (`claude mcp add`), and the examples default to Anthropic models, although other agents and LLM providers are mentioned.

scenarios.name: structured-laptop-extraction
scenarios.rationale: Both define Pydantic Laptop and wrapper models, pass the wrapper via output_model_schema, read history.structured_output, use browser_use's ChatAnthropic, and set max_steps on agent.run(), so both meet the rubric and differ only in extras such as B's exact-five validation and A's allowed_domains.

scenarios.name: login-headless-ci-secrets
scenarios.rationale: B follows the rubric: it keeps the password out of the task text, logs in once and exports with export_storage_state, reuses auth.json via Browser(headless=True, storage_state=...), sets allowed_domains and max_steps, and gitignores auth.json and stores it as a CI secret. A uses sensitive_data with a TOTP secret in CI, explicitly advises against persisting storage_state, and never mentions export_storage_state, so it misses the core recommendation, though it does set allowed_domains and max_steps.

scenarios.name: custom-2fa-tool-and-verify
scenarios.rationale: Both use Tools() with @tools.action returning ActionResult(extracted_content=...), pass tools=, use is_done/is_successful/errors/number_of_steps, and warn that the success flag is the agent's own claim; B is more thorough, with a stop-reason report and an explicit URL assertion, but it hedges about the old Controller and its action description is passed positionally, while A states the caveat clearly in a table and bullets and passes description= as the rubric specifies.
